svg.text: Part 2 — CI/CD Pipeline for the Auto Scaling Backend (role-free design)
GitHub Actions → GitHub Release → pull-based deploy onto the Auto Scaling fleet · Blue/Green via ALB listener switch | Joyanta Sarker Joy · Mastering DevOps (Batch 13)
3 DEPLOY (AWS ap-south-1, no IAM roles needed)
edits app/, bumps version in package.json
git commit && git push origin main
public → servers can fetch releases without credentials
Repo contents used by the pipeline
runs on: push to main (app/**) or manual dispatch
any failing test stops the pipeline — nothing is released
listener HTTP :80 → default action = forward to ONE target group
New instance (scale-out or self-healing) → Launch Template user-data
→ runs deploy.sh AT BOOT → same version as the fleet before its first health check
shared by BLUE and GREEN (same data, no migration in this lab)
Flow: ① push → ② build + test + package + release → ③ every server pulls its track (BLUE=latest, GREEN=pinned) → ④ ALB listener decides who gets traffic → rollback = point the listener back at BLUE
Legend: solid = live traffic / active pull · dashed = standby path (used during Blue/Green switch) · orange dashed box = Auto Scaling Group · yellow = artifact / release

Security: every arrow into AWS is OUTBOUND from the servers over HTTPS 443 (default security-group egress). No IAM role, instance profile, access key, or extra inbound port is needed anywhere in this pipeline.
